paragraphs: Dre’Kaar gives the Commander Beetle three orders. Latve must wake everyone, Faelina must set the traps, and Narion must move from the left flank to the right lookout after Dre’Kaar spots an apparent orc advance. Each order is an object that carries its own receiver and knows what to ask that receiver to do.

Three child beetles register with the Commander Beetle, one for each order. When Dre’Kaar chooses an order, the Commander sends a copy of the corresponding beetle and keeps the registered beetle beside her. The Commander says execute() to the child beetle. The copy flies to its receiver and calls that receiver’s method to carry out the order.

Once Narion reaches the right lookout, the orcs withdraw on the right and Dre’Kaar sees the real attack on the left. The command saved Narion’s previous post when it ran. Undo sends him back to defend the left flank.
imageAlt: Dre’Kaar riding a large beetle with golden wings
task: Build the class diagram for the three orders. Show how Dre’Kaar hands them to the Commander Beetle and how each order delegates work to its receiver.
concept: The Command pattern encapsulates a request in an object. The invoker uses the same execute() interface for every order, so it can queue and run different requests without knowing the receiver’s methods. An application can also keep a history and support undo for commands that know how to reverse their effects.
steps: Identify the client, invoker, commands, and receivers
Connect the invoker to Command and each concrete order to its receiver
Execute Narion’s order, then undo it to restore his previous post
